info.title: CAWG-TRQP Reference Verifier HTTP API
info.description:
This is the OpenAPI specification of the HTTP API exposed by cawg-trqp-refimpl, the CAWG-TRQP reference verifier (https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/cawg-trqp-verifier-refimpl and its TypeScript port). It is a request/response reference implementation for evaluating CAWG/C2PA manifest trust signals against TRQP-style policy: authorization and issuer-recognition lookups against a configurable PolicyService (an in-memory mock, or a real Redis/MongoDB/MySQL/Postgres-backed plugin), full manifest verification combining asset integrity, authorization, recognition, and process-proof appraisal, and signed/replayable audit bundle export.

This API is intentionally narrower than the CAWG Trust Registry Resolution API described elsewhere in this specification: it is POST-with-body rather than resource-oriented REST, it has no entity enrollment flow, no historical (atTime) authorization queries, no array-variant combined-permission check, and no capability-discovery routes for listing an authority's recognized actions/resources. It documents an existing reference tool rather than prescribing the API a conformant Trust Registry must expose.

servers.description: Default local address used by the bundled CLI/scripts/start_http_service.ts

tags.name: Authorization
tags.description: Direct authorization and issuer-recognition lookups against the configured PolicyService

tags.name: Gateway
tags.description: Authorization/recognition lookups mediated through a TrustGateway

get.summary: Reports service health and enabled capabilities
get.description: Returns the service's health status and the list of capabilities (authorization, recognition, verify, audit_bundle, gateway) this deployment has enabled. Unauthenticated; intended for load balancer / orchestrator health checks.

post.summary: Checks whether an entity is authorized to perform an action on a resource
post.description: Given entity_id, authority_id, action, and resource, returns whether the entity is currently authorized, drawn from the configured PolicyService. This reference API always evaluates against the policy data as currently configured; it has no equivalent of a historical (atTime) query.

400.description: Invalid request (missing/invalid fields, unknown profile or overlay name)

413.description: Request body exceeds the service's configured size limit (64KB by default)

502.description: The configured PolicyService backend failed to complete the request (e.g. a network/database error from a real backend plugin)

post.summary: Checks whether one Governing Authority recognizes another as a trusted issuer
post.description: Given authority_id and recognized_authority_id, returns whether the first authority recognizes the second as a trusted issuer of identity assertions, drawn from the configured PolicyService.

400.description: Invalid request (missing/invalid fields, unknown profile or overlay name)

413.description: Request body exceeds the service's configured size limit (64KB by default)

502.description: The configured PolicyService backend failed to complete the request (e.g. a network/database error from a real backend plugin)

post.summary: Checks authorization through a trust gateway, returning route mediation evidence
post.description: Equivalent to POST /trqp/authorization, but routes the query through a TrustGateway that can mediate requests across multiple configured authority routes, returning route/feed-descriptor evidence describing how the request was mediated alongside the authorization result.

400.description: Invalid request (missing/invalid fields, unknown profile or overlay name)

413.description: Request body exceeds the service's configured size limit (64KB by default)

502.description: The configured PolicyService backend failed to complete the request (e.g. a network/database error from a real backend plugin)

post.summary: Verifies a CAWG/C2PA manifest's asset integrity, actor authorization, issuer recognition, and process integrity
post.description: Performs a full verification pass combining asset integrity, actor authorization, issuer recognition, and (if process_evidence is supplied) process-proof appraisal, returning a structured trust_outcome (trusted, trusted_cached, rejected, or deferred) with explanations.

400.description: Invalid request (missing/invalid fields, unknown profile or overlay name)

413.description: Request body exceeds the service's configured size limit (64KB by default)

502.description: The configured PolicyService backend failed to complete the request (e.g. a network/database error from a real backend plugin)

post.summary: Verifies a manifest and exports a signed, replayable audit bundle of the decision
post.description: Runs the same verification pass as POST /trqp/verify, then packages the request, result, and policy evidence into a canonical, hashable audit bundle suitable for replay and independent re-verification later.

parameters.name: X-TRQP-Scopes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of scopes granted to the caller. Required to include the privacy_profile's access_scope whenever privacy_profile retains the raw request (replay_bundle, regulated_evidence); otherwise the request is rejected with 403. This reference implementation has no authentication middleware - the header is trusted as presented.

403.description: privacy_profile requires a scope not present in X-TRQP-Scopes

400.description: Invalid request (missing/invalid fields, unknown profile or overlay name)

413.description: Request body exceeds the service's configured size limit (64KB by default)

502.description: The configured PolicyService backend failed to complete the request (e.g. a network/database error from a real backend plugin)

error.description: Machine-readable error code, e.g. invalid_request, forbidden, upstream_unavailable, request_too_large

entity_id.description: Identifier of the actor/entity claiming to have performed the action, matching the entity identifier recorded in the manifest

authority_id.description: Identifier of the Governing Authority whose policy governs this action/resource

action.description: The action being authorized, e.g. publish

resource.description: The resource category the action applies to, e.g. cawg:news-content

context.description: Additional policy-matching context (e.g. jurisdiction, risk_tier). Policy rules match when every key they declare is present with an equal value in this context; the request may carry extra keys a rule doesn't mention

cawgtrqp.authorizationResponse.description: Fields other than authorized are omitted from the actual JSON response whenever their value is null (this schema lists them as optional, not nullable, to reflect that omission)

authority_id.description: The authority whose recognition policy is being queried

recognized_authority_id.description: The authority (typically an issuer) being checked for recognition

context.description: Additional policy-matching context (e.g. jurisdiction, risk_tier). Policy rules match when every key they declare is present with an equal value in this context; the request may carry extra keys a rule doesn't mention

cawgtrqp.recognitionResponse.description: Fields other than recognized are omitted from the actual JSON response whenever their value is null

asset_id.description: Identifier of the asset (e.g. image, article) this manifest is about

integrity_ok.description: Whether the manifest's own cryptographic integrity (signature/hash chain) already validated, prior to calling this service. If false, verification short-circuits to a rejected asset_integrity result

entity_id.description: Identifier of the actor/entity claiming to have performed the action, matching the entity identifier recorded in the manifest

authority_id.description: Identifier of the Governing Authority whose policy governs this action/resource

issuer_id.description: Identifier of the certificate issuer vouching for entity_id, if any. When present, issuer recognition is checked against authority_id's recognition policy

action.description: The action being authorized, e.g. publish

resource.description: The resource category the action applies to, e.g. cawg:news-content

context.description: Additional policy-matching context (e.g. jurisdiction, risk_tier). Policy rules match when every key they declare is present with an equal value in this context; the request may carry extra keys a rule doesn't mention

process_evidence.description: Optional Proof-of-Process style evidence describing how the asset was produced, appraised against the matched policy's process requirements (requires_process_proof, min_process_integrity, allowed_process_types)

profile.description: Selects a verification profile: either a built-in profile name (edge, standard, high_assurance), or a fully inline profile payload matching the verification-profile schema for a one-off custom profile. Defaults to "standard".

oneOf.description: Inline verification profile. See verification-profile.schema.json in the cawg-trqp-refimpl schemas/ directory for the full controls shape.

overlays.description: Built-in overlay names to layer onto the resolved profile's controls, applied in order. Only built-in names are accepted at this API boundary (evidence_attested, freshness_strict) - filesystem paths are rejected.

use_gateway.description: When true, routes the authorization/recognition lookups through the configured TrustGateway instead of calling the PolicyService directly

process_integrity.description: e.g. not_required, verified, verified_high, insufficient, failed, missing_required_proof

policy_freshness.description: e.g. fresh, stale_but_warned, revoked, service_unavailable, service_error, snapshot_verified

verification_mode.description: e.g. cached_online, online_full, gateway_mediated, offline_snapshot, revocation_check, transport_guardrail

policy_evidence.description: Includes the resolved verification_profile, transport metadata, revocation_status, and feed_descriptors evidence used to reach this result

gateway_mediation.description: Populated only when use_gateway was true

asset_id.description: Identifier of the asset (e.g. image, article) this manifest is about

action.description: The action being authorized, e.g. publish

resource.description: The resource category the action applies to, e.g. cawg:news-content

context.description: Additional policy-matching context (e.g. jurisdiction, risk_tier). Policy rules match when every key they declare is present with an equal value in this context; the request may carry extra keys a rule doesn't mention

process_evidence.description: Optional Proof-of-Process style evidence describing how the asset was produced, appraised against the matched policy's process requirements (requires_process_proof, min_process_integrity, allowed_process_types)

oneOf.description: Inline verification profile. See verification-profile.schema.json in the cawg-trqp-refimpl schemas/ directory for the full controls shape.

overlays.description: Built-in overlay names to layer onto the resolved profile's controls, applied in order. Only built-in names are accepted at this API boundary (evidence_attested, freshness_strict) - filesystem paths are rejected.

privacy_profile.description: Controls how much of the raw request is retained in the exported bundle. minimal_receipt pseudonymizes identifiers; replay_bundle and regulated_evidence retain the raw request and require the caller to present the profile's access_scope in the X-TRQP-Scopes header, or the request is rejected with 403

bundle_id.description: urn:trqp:audit-bundle:sha256:<digest of the bundle's canonical content>

replay_inputs.description: Pinned policy/revocation feed digests, transport metadata, and the resolved profile, sufficient to independently replay this decision later

bundle_attestation.description: Present only when the bundle was signed

value.description: Base64-encoded Ed25519 signature over the bundle's canonical content
